name: Tuerong
intro: Tuerong is where some of the Peninsula's best bottles come from roads most visitors never take. Yabby Lake is the anchor - Halliday Top 100, relaxed cellar-door program - and the same back roads hold Dexter Wines and a cluster of low-volume producers whose fruit ends up in Melbourne's better wine lists. Quiet, specific, worth the detour.
factualLede: Tuerong is a rural hinterland locality on the Mornington Peninsula's northern wine country, 70 km from Melbourne, known for the Quealy Winemakers cellar door and the Devilbend Reservoir.

heroImage.alt: Tuerong vineyard rows running down toward a quiet farm road

tldr: Tuerong is a rural locality best known to wine enthusiasts as the address of Yabby Lake Vineyard and Dromana Estate.
Best for: serious wine visitors; walkers at Devilbend Reservoir; travellers who want hinterland quiet without driving all the way to Red Hill.
Half a day; usually paired with Moorooduc or Mornington.
notFor: people wanting a village to walk around
signature: The wine-country back door, where some of the Peninsula's best bottles come from roads most visitors never take.
skip: Dropping in without knowing where you are headed - Tuerong only works if you choose the wineries in advance.
bestDay: Yabby Lake late morning, one more tasting nearby, lunch with a vineyard view, Devilbend walk if there is still daylight.
insiderNote: This is the pocket where Melbourne sommeliers buy wine, which tells you more than any brochure will.
